name: Wynonna
notes: The archetype's blues-and-gospel wing on 90s radio — a huge contralto with R&B phrasing over a band that plays shuffles, gospel 12/8 and blues frames rather than two-beats. The 1980s duo era is excluded under Gate 2 and the modelled window is the solo run, 1992–2003, exactly as the entry states. The drum instruction is explicit and is what sets this model apart from every other in the section: "the mid band runs a shuffled feel with the lope on hat or ride and a heavier, more R&B-scaled backbeat than any other entry in this section … Model more kick weight and more snare compression than the honky-tonk norm." More weight and more compression are authored as the highest velocity tiers here (114–127 accent over an 86–104 main — a raised floor is what compression does) with humanize's velocityVar pulled down to 0.16, plus a busier kick (syncopation 0.18, offbeat8thShare 0.12) and a much busier hat (0.44 fill, open hat 0.26). The gospel cuts are documented as adding "tambourine on the backbeat and hand-claps", which is the steady tambourine at −3 dB plus a clap layered on the backbeat snare through `snare.layerClapOffsetMs` — the hand-claps cannot be a percs lane, because `clap` is not in the engine's `PERC_LANES` (engine/src/generators/drums.rs) and would be dropped, and a `snap` lane would play finger snaps instead of the documented claps. Harmony is the entry's own: twelve-bar blues including the sourced seventh-chord elaboration, gospel I–IV–I–V with ♭III and ♭VII borrowings written as their own degrees, and ii–V–I turnarounds; extensions run 0.34/0.5/0.16. The bass is stated to be "mixed forward and playing a genuine *line* rather than a pattern — walking, syncopated, with anticipations before the downbeat, i.e. an R&B bass idiom inside a country arrangement", so independent_riff at 0.6 with the batch's highest anticipationProb, 0.38. The vocal is "a very large contralto with wide range, heavy melisma, blues-scale ornaments, growled attacks and full-voice sustained peaks" and the entry states the arrangement consequence — it "must leave real dynamic headroom". The gospel/R&B "vamp-out with ad-libs" that the entry calls in-grammar here and rare elsewhere in country is the 8–16-bar outro. ⚠ INFERRED: swing.amount 0.66, all velocity tiers, ghost probability and vel, hat and percs densities, and the clap's 2–6 ms offset off the snare — that number is phase avoidance rather than a research fact (`country-pop` ships 1–3 ms for a programmed clap; these are hands in a room). Fourteen per-track BPM readings support the 55–209 band and the stated 81–118 identity band (mode 100 is "No One Else on Earth"), but they are bpmdatabase values and [LOW-CONF] as a class; the research also marks the per-track harmony as generalised [LOW-CONF]. The dance remixes at 128–140 the entry names are explicitly not modelled.
